items.title: A new discrete log attack landed
items.oneliner: A deterministic subexponential discrete log algorithm just landed, which puts old cryptographic comfort assumptions under real pressure.

items.title: OpenAI pushed matrix multiplication theory forward
items.oneliner: OpenAI's tensor preprint claims a new matrix multiplication lower bound, which matters because AI scaling still runs on linear algebra.

items.title: DeepL cut voice translation lag
items.oneliner: DeepL says Aure v2 halves voice translation latency, which is the kind of UX gain that actually changes product adoption.

items.title: States sued xAI over Grok imagery
items.oneliner: Virginia and Oregon sued xAI over Grok image generation, turning AI safety failures into an enforcement problem.

items.title: WebRTC skimmers hit shopping sites
items.oneliner: WebRTC-based card skimmers were found on major shopping sites before Black Friday, proving browser abuse keeps evolving faster than defenses.

items.title: Convex skill leaked user app ideas
items.oneliner: A Convex skill reportedly sent user app ideas to a remote server without notice, which is a trust-killer for agent tooling.

items.title: Self-hosted email is back on the table
items.oneliner: The Dutch government and ICC examples make one point clear: outsourced email is now a sovereignty and resilience risk.

items.title: Garage added a real web admin
items.oneliner: Garage 2.6.0 shipped a web admin UI, making S3-compatible self-hosted object storage much more realistic for smaller teams.

items.title: Rust finally stabilized custom allocators
items.oneliner: Rust 1.100 stabilizes the allocator API, giving performance-sensitive teams first-class control over memory behavior instead of hacks.

items.title: Tiny Hat targets retro game development
items.oneliner: Tiny Hat ships a sub-100MB Linux distro for retro gamedev, which is niche but unusually practical systems engineering.
